changes.text: The source tree is reorganised around how you would look for things: the preview windows moved out of the repo root into previews/ behind a small router, and the jargon names became the words you would actually search for - Notifications, Calculator, SystemInfo, SummonZone, the alphabet launcher, SquircleRect. Nothing about how the shell looks or behaves moved with them.

The shell is now fully legible to the QML language server: every folder carries a qmldir and the LSP's import path is wired up, so code completion finds your own singletons and the editor's warning floor went from thousands to the few that can be kept honest. If you add a QML file, run scripts/qmldirs.sh once.
Internal: the source code shed its comment essays, cut to bare minimum, with no change to anything the shell does. Your config and setup are untouched; anyone reading the code can read it again.

Bare mode now squares the windows too (rounding and both gaps, outer and inner, go to zero), and the shell applies the compositor half itself: on the toggle, on every boot, and again after every compositor reload while bare, so the state comes back from a reboot whole instead of half-applied. Toggling back reloads the compositor, which returns your config's gaps and rounding to every open window at once.

Bare mode: the whole chrome can go off at once, every screen. Band, sidebar, reserved space and the invisible edge grabs all stand down, leaving the wallpaper and your windows; the shell still answers every keybind. Super+Shift+K toggles it, and runs the compositor's gap flip beside it so the windows sit flush.
One new config.json key, edge.bare, holds the switch. It is off by default and your config gains it by itself; nothing to do.

The sidebar can now be hidden on individual monitors. The Monitors page has a Sidebar switch for the selected one, and Super+K toggles the column on the monitor you are on; hidden means fully, with the windows taking the width back.

Two new config.json keys hold the same setting: sidebar.enabled, the default every screen follows, and sidebar.perScreen, which holds only the monitors that disagree. Your config gains them by itself; nothing to do.
